stem:
Priya fills a plastic syringe with air and closes its opening tightly with her finger. When she pushes the plunger in, the air inside is compressed into a smaller volume.

Why can the air in the closed syringe be compressed?

options.text: The air particles themselves shrink when the plunger is pushed.
The air particles are far apart with large spaces between them, so they can be forced closer together.
The air particles change into liquid particles when pushed together.
The air particles escape through the walls of the syringe.

teacher.key_rationale: Gases are compressible because their particles have large interparticle spaces; pushing the plunger forces the particles closer together, reducing the volume. A is wrong because particles do not change size; C is wrong because no change of state occurs; D contradicts the closed opening.
